method: Independent model linguistic review of every candidate, English sense and supplied Spanish semantic evidence. Frames are reviewed selected-sense derivatives, not verbatim dictionary translations or native-human certification. Only the first English verb may be inflected; no implicit clitic, missing middle object, qualified irregular override or invented Spanish paradigm is approved. Preserve per-reading context, region/register and source warnings. Aspect modes authorize only a selected contextual reading and remain subject to source grammar/person and verified English inflection guards.

rejected.reason: Source points to acodarse and an elbow-supporting pronominal construction; do not drop the required clitic.
Pronominal-only root acodarse needs independently validated clitic rendering, not a bare-root substitution.
English making friends and Spanish causing two people to become friends have different argument structures; no safe fixed frame established.
English embolden is causative, whereas retained Spanish atrever evidence is acting boldly or a reflexive construction; role alignment unresolved.
Rare recudir readings return/pay lack a retained Spanish semantic gloss and sufficiently confident sense alignment.
Putting someone on a diet needs an object before the complement; bare diet would reverse the selected subject role.
English felt-like versus Spanish plush/felpa texture is insufficiently aligned; a make-object-textured frame also has a middle object slot.
Sink has causative/inchoative ambiguity and retained constructions do not establish one safe subject-preserving frame.
English explicitly describes air-current winnowing while Spanish describes sieving with a harnero; do not erase the method mismatch.
English chipping an edge versus Spanish loss of an instrument edge leaves causative/inchoative roles unresolved.
Head-lowering gloss requires a subject-bound possessor; retained Spanish lacks a clarifying gloss and no safe fixed frame established.
Regional lift/bend-up English sense is not corroborated by retained Spanish nautical reefing/fastening senses.
English line-up troops implies arrangement; Spanish explicitly gathers people in disorder. Do not merge those meanings.
Specialized vine-bending sense has no retained Spanish semantic gloss; technical alignment remains uncertain.
Distinct rare animal-limping, string-noise and resistance senses lack retained Spanish semantic clarification.
English drop down a well can assign falling to the subject; Spanish puts an object in a well. A safe middle-object frame is required.
Unresolved encentar cross-reference provides no independently established semantic frame in this batch.
Unresolved rizar cross-reference without retained semantic gloss; no sense-specific frame confidently established.
English getting oneself into a mess does not align with retained wind-noise/annoyance definitions or subject roles.
Grain/sow glosses leave plant production, seed sowing and grain processing unresolved; retained Spanish is no-gloss.
English match borrowing is not corroborated by retained Spanish breeding/pollination meanings; this spelling and sense remain uncertain.
English beat is semantically ambiguous, while retained Spanish gives architectural montea drawing; no reliable shared frame selected.
Father-resemblance frame requires a subject-bound possessive and the other rare sense lacks sufficient independent confirmation.
Obscure retail-price allocation sense lacks a retained Spanish gloss or sufficiently confident argument alignment.
English rebel describes the actor, while Spanish rebelar makes others rebel; do not silently replace a causative with an intransitive.
English tying/shaking grain differs from Spanish drawing a rope over crops to remove dew; other rope-measuring sense remains uncertain.
Derogatory English gloss does not reliably distinguish sexual activity, sex work and client roles; Spanish retained evidence has no clarifying gloss.
Unresolved chapuzar cross-reference with no retained semantic gloss; no safe causative/intransitive selection established.
English merit/deserve presents an entity deserving something; Spanish describes acting meritoriously. Do not conflate the state with its acquisition/action.
English bronze is not a safe synonym for the familiar steel-blue pavonar coating process; retained Spanish lacks a clarifying gloss.
Both English senses are reflexive self-pride/self-valuation, whereas retained Spanish is rare transitive apreciar; no clitic-safe match.
Unresolved arregazar cross-reference; no selected independent semantic frame established.
Both supplied senses require body parts belonging to the subject; fixed one's would not agree with generated persons and no possessive-aware renderer is authorized.
Assuming a title/right makes the subject recipient, while retained Spanish assigning/conferring makes it giver; reflexive arrogation requires clitic evidence.
English tipping a ship on its side and Spanish repairing its hull are related but distinct actions; do not imply one from the other.
English restraining/moderating is not supported by the retained obsolete Spanish thinking/planning sense.
English keystoning is not equivalent to cutting every stone into a wedge-shaped voussoir; architectural action mismatch.
Obsolete remanir has no Spanish semantic evidence here and its retire/remain/withdraw distinctions are not confidently established.
Step back, step again and memorize are distinct senses without retained Spanish clarification; no sufficiently confident selected mapping.
English crowding together is reflexive; Spanish nonpronominal sense causes others to gather. Do not reverse subject roles or omit required se.
Lighting a cigarette differs from retained Spanish striking flint to create sparks; no specific shared action confidently established.
English explicitly planing wood and Spanish working it with an adze-like doladera use different methods; withhold this tool-specific mismatch.
English regional choke is not corroborated by Spanish putting draught animals in a yoke or fitting a bell yoke; construction and sense uncertain.
